material_gaps: Legal classification: amending order whose inserted sentence was restated by EO 13683 is not expressly ended; owner or reviewer criterion needed.
notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 12080 (43 FR 42235, Sept 18, 1978): adds one sentence to section 4 of EO 11030 on commemorative proclamations. I read the held EO 13683 (79 FR 75041), whose section 1(b) restates section 4 of EO 11030 'to read as follows' with a modified version of the same sentence ('the Director or the head of such designated office, as appropriate, shall transmit any approved commemorative proclamations to the President'); EO 12608 and 13403 amend other sections. So the text added by EO 12080 no longer exists as written. No held instrument revokes or names EO 12080, and the 1 CFR part 19 authority citation and 44 U.S.C. 1505 note still cite it as an amender. Whether an amending order whose inserted text has been replaced by a later restatement should be status NO is a legal-classification question that is not decided by the held text; I lean NO but I do not treat it as an unresolved reading of sources I can finish. Blocked as an unresolved legal-classification conflict; the restatement text is already held (ACT:EO:12080>EO:13683) so no fetch is needed.
